summary: Georgia agriculture commissioner and governor Eugene Talmadge ruled through martial law, old executive loopholes and the National Guard in the 1930s and 1940s, crushed textile strikes, purged educators over integration and campaigned on open white supremacy until his death in 1946.
keywords: The Wild Man from Sugar Creek

anti-FDR Grassroots Convention under Confederate flags with racist literature
fires the comptroller and treasurer in 1936; guardsmen carry the treasurer out
refuses to concede the 1938 Senate loss and alleges voter fraud
